# The site — orientation for a session working on banyan.city

Written 2026-08-03 because a second Claude Code tab was being opened to work on the
website, and `CLAUDE.md` covers the rules and the render pipeline but says almost
nothing about how the site is built. Everything a web-facing session needs is here
or linked from here. **Read `CLAUDE.md` first anyway** — the reserved list applies to
you too.

## The one thing to understand first

**There is no framework and no `src/`.** The site is generated by one Python script,
`pipeline/build_site.py` (~1700 lines), which reads the genome files and writes
static HTML into `_site/`. `_site/` is **gitignored** — it is a build artifact, never
edited by hand, and regenerating it is the only way to change the site.

```bash
python3 pipeline/build_site.py      # genomes -> _site/, ~seconds, no network
open _site/index.html               # look at it locally
```

If you edit HTML in `_site/`, your change disappears on the next build. Edit
`build_site.py` (structure/markup) or `pipeline/site_theme.py` (~190 lines: colours,
type, spacing) instead.

## Pages it emits

| file | what it is |
|---|---|
| `index.html` | the front door |
| `watch.html`, `watch/season.html` | the episode viewer |
| `season.html` | season overview |
| `city.html` | the city/world page |
| `create.html` | the contribution route — see "the main artifact" below |
| `machine.html` | how the machine works, publicly |
| `<genome>/<node>-shots.html` | per-node shot board, one page per node |
| `trials/index.html` | the T3 provider trials |
| `review/index.html` | **unlisted** — working cuts the author has not passed, for his screening (D17). `noindex`, absent from the nav, linked only from his inbox on the status page. Content comes from `cuts/cuts.yaml`; the mp4s in `cuts/` are the one place media is committed |

Page builders worth knowing in `build_site.py`: `page()` (the shell every page
uses), `render_node_page()`, `node_card()`, `chips()`, `trunk_chain()`,
`live_videos()`, `audio_credits()`.

## Two rules that are not style opinions

**1. `publishable()` decides what reaches the site, and it is a licence gate.**
`build_site.py` has `publishable()`, `public_licence()` and `withheld_note()`. Assets
whose model licence cannot pass through our CC BY 4.0 offer are *withheld from the
published page* rather than shown. Do not route around it to make a page look
fuller — that function existing is the reason an unpublishable clip has never
shipped. The current debt is tracked by `pipeline/licence_gate.py` and asserted as a
count in `lint_genome.py`.

**2. The site must not claim things it cannot know.** `build_sim.py`'s status page
was reworded from "In production right now" to "as of this snapshot" with a UTC
footer, because a static page cannot update itself and was stating a live fact. Same
discipline applies anywhere you write present-tense copy.

## The main artifact, per the founder

The crowd-contribution system — the shot board and the fork-per-beat route — is the
product, not a feature of it. Full transparency is the point: the repo IS the
product. If a design choice trades away legibility of *how it was made*, that is the
wrong trade. Relevant: `create.html`, the shot boards, `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

## Deploy

Push to `main` and the **GitHub Pages** mirror (`pages.yml`) rebuilds. It runs
`lint_genome.py` **before** `build_site.py`, so a lint failure stops the site
deploying, not just a badge. Also `lint.yml`, `mirror.yml`, `sap.yml`.
**Check CI after pushing** (`gh run list`); CI has been red while local passed
before.

**Vercel is disconnected right now.** Dad removed banyan-city from his Vercel
account on 2026-08-07 after it billed **>$100 in under a month** — 500+ build
hours, almost none of it the site changing. The cause: each farm box
force-pushes a heartbeat commit to its own `farm-results-*` branch every ~5
minutes, and every one of those was a Vercel deployment running the full pip
install + `build_site.py`. Roughly 1,150 builds a day to publish nothing. The
domain move to a new account is work orders **V6–V9 in `OPERATOR.md`**.

Before that connection is made again, three layers have to be in place, and
only the first two are code:

1. **`vercel.json` → `git.deploymentEnabled`** — deny-all, `main` only. Vercel
   evaluates this *before* creating a deployment, so a non-main push produces no
   event at all. This is the layer that actually kills the farm-branch flood.
2. **`pipeline/vercel-ignore-build.sh`** (wired up as `ignoreCommand`) — even on
   `main`, exits 0/skip unless the push changed a path `build_site.py` actually
   reads. The header comment lists every path and why. Note honestly what it
   *cannot* do: a skipped build is still a triggered-then-skipped **deployment
   event** and still takes a concurrent build slot — near-zero build minutes, not
   zero events.
3. **Project settings on Vercel's side** — Production Branch = `main`, preview
   deployments off, on-demand concurrency off, Standard build machine. Settings
   are the only layer that governs a branch whose checked-out `vercel.json` is
   stale, which force-pushed farm branches are. Those clicks are V8.

**And layer 3 is doing more work than it sounds like — measured 2026-08-08.**
Vercel reads `git.deploymentEnabled` from the config in *the commit being
pushed*, so it only governs a branch that carries it. Right now **none of the
four `farm-results-*` branches do**: they are up to 93 commits behind main with
the pre-guard `vercel.json`. The same staleness is already observable in
Actions — three of the four still carry the pre-2026-08-06 `lint.yml` with no
`branches-ignore`, which is why `lint-genome` and `mirror` still fire on every
five-minute heartbeat despite that fix having landed on main two days ago.

They do heal, on their own, but only partly. `farm_worker.py:573` runs
`git checkout -q origin/main -- .` before each task, so a courier branch picks
up main's *modified* files — including the guarded `vercel.json` — on its next
task cycle. It never picks up *deletions*: those branches will keep carrying the
deleted `.github/workflows/vercel.yml` indefinitely. Harmless (it is the same
no-op that never deployed), but it will not clear itself, and until each branch
turns over, the dashboard settings are the only thing standing between a courier
heartbeat and a build.

There is no `vercel` GitHub Actions workflow any more — it was deleted
2026-08-08, having never deployed once in 100 runs (see V4). Vercel git
integration needs no workflow and no secret in this repo.

## Reading order for a site session

1. `CLAUDE.md` — auto-loaded, non-negotiable rules
2. `PROMISE.md` (11 lines, canonical) and `README.md` (the map)
3. This file
4. `pipeline/site_theme.py` — small, and tells you the visual system
5. `build_site.py` — only the function you need; it is long
6. `DECISIONS.md` for anything that looks like it was already argued about

`STATE.md` is 573 lines of running log. Skim the last entries; do not read it all.

## Coordination — this matters if two tabs are open

Two sessions in one working tree collide: same files, same index, same branch. If a
render session is active it is committing and pushing to `main` continuously.

- **Preferred:** the site session takes its own git worktree, so the two never share
  an index.
- **Otherwise:** agree an explicit file boundary and stick to it. A site session
  touches `build_site.py`, `site_theme.py`, `*.md` copy. It should not touch
  `pipeline/farm-queue.yaml`, `video_task.py`, `wan_i2v.py`, `motion.yaml` or
  anything under `genomes/*/nodes/*/clips/`.
- **Either way:** `git pull --rebase` before committing, and expect the other
  session to have moved `main`.

## Founder-reserved (from `CLAUDE.md`, repeated because it is easy to trip on here)

Posting or announcing on the founder's accounts, spending money, credential changes,
taste-axis scores and trunk/graft calls, governance changes, opening money rails.
A site session will be tempted by the first one — building a share button is fine,
pressing it is not.
